1.  CALL TO ORDER

  A regular meeting of the Traffic Commission of the City of Rolling Hills was called to order by
  Chair Wilson at 8:30 a.m. on Thursday, November 21, 2019 in the City Council Chamber, at City
  Hall, 2 Portuguese Bend Road, Rolling Hills, California.

2.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Hawkins, Margeta, Raine, Virtue and Chair Wilson
  Commissioners Absent:  None
  Others Present:  Yolanta Schwartz, Planning Director
  Meredith T. Elguira, Planning & Community Services Director
  Yohana Coronel, City Clerk
  Vanessa Munoz, Traffic Engineer
  Deputy Tami Bouse
  Kristen Raig, RHCA Manager
  Arty Beckler, RHCA Maintenance Supervisor

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  OCTOBER 3, 2019 MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE TRAFFIC
  COMMISSION.

  Commissioner Margeta clarified that a question was not asked as to why thermoplastics should
  be used, it was a statement that the Traffic Commission should review with the Caballeros if it’s
  still wanted.

  Traffic Engineer Vanessa Munoz clarified that on Page 3, 7th paragraph it’s stated that thermos
  should not be used at crossing but on edge line and on page 4, section B, 2nd paragraph, she
  wanted to say that the driveway is acceptable, not normal.

  Commissioner Virtue moved that the Traffic Commission approve the minutes of the regular
  meeting of the Traffic Commission held on October 03, 2019 with grammatical changes to be
  made on page 2 and Commissioner Margeta seconded the motion to approve the minutes.

  AYES:  Commissioners: Margeta, Raine, Virtue and Chairman Wilson
  NOES:  None.
  ABSENT:  None.
  ABSTAIN:  Commissioner: Hawkins

4.  PRESENTATION

  4
   A.  PRESENTATION BY REPRESENTATIVES OF THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  SHERIFF’S DEPARTMENT, LOMITA STATION, ON TRAFFIC STATISTICS
  FOR THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS.

  Deputy Tami Bouse gave an overview of the traffic statistics for the City of Rolling Hills for
  July, August, and September. In July, there were 32 cites, 19 supplemental, one with unsafe entry
  on the highway from a driveway. In August, there were 24 cites, 14 supplemental, one stop sign
  and the rest were speeding. In September, there were 35 cites, 43 supplemental, one juvenile
  cited. The month of September was busy because of start of the school year. Highest speed
  recorded was 54 MPH. There was one warrant arrest and one arrest for suspended license. There
  was one accident on Saddleback that took out an archway on a driveway but no information on
  the second accident. Deputy Bouse offered to send a copy of report involving the second accident.
  The first of the contract covered July to November, second phase in December and third phase
  begins in January. There were 16 hours that could be carried over to December. Deputy Bouse
  recommended a carryover from Phase 1 to Phase 2.

  Chair Wilson emphasized the need to cover back to school and the holiday period.

  Deputy Bouse mentioned that they will keep trying but it would be better to reallocate
  supplemental when traffic picks up again.

  Commissioner Hawkins claimed that there were speeders between 4:30 and 6 PM on Crest Road.

  Deputy Bouse claimed that she had a hard time finding speeders. Deputy Bouse explained that
  citing speeders on Crest Road West would be pushing it.

  Rolling Hills Community Association Manager Kristen Raig brought up that kids will be home
  from school so she suggested taking that into consideration.

  Deputy Bouse mentioned that people will also be out of town. She also mentioned that sheriff
  staff will not be available during the holidays but she will try to get a Deputy to come and
  monitor.

  Chair Wilson deferred to Deputy Bouse for best judgment.

  Deputy Bouse agreed she will try to have someone monitor for the first part of Thanksgiving
  week but cannot guarantee availability during Thanksgiving holiday. Deputy Bouse stated that
  she stays for an hour but if no citations were issued, the City was not billed for her time.

  Commissioner Hawkins brought up that there were no cites after 4:30 in the afternoon concluding
  that there might not have been a presence of a Deputy after 4:30 PM.

  Commissioner Hawkins also brought up parking concern under RHMC 10.52.140 relating to
  parking on equestrian path. He cited that no parking is allowed on equestrian paths so as to cause
  equestrians to use the road instead of such trail or path.

   Commissioner Hawkins showed photographs of what he described as egregious parking on Crest
  Road. He noted that he was not aware of anyone ever being cited for parking violation. He added
  that it was dangerous for equestrians and pedestrians to be forced off the bridle trail onto the
  roadway; the risk of fatal accident was heightened.

  Commissioner Hawkins asked Deputy Bouse if something could be done to more vigorously

  Chair Wilson brought up that signage would be needed if people are to be cited for the violation.

  Planning Director Yolanta Schwartz interjected and brought up that this item needed to be

  to allow parking on trails during construction.

  Chair Wilson agreed to bring this topic up at a future meeting.

  B.  CONSIDER A REQUEST FROM ROLLING HILLS COMMUNITY
  ASSOCIATION TO RELOCATE THE BARRIER ARMS AND STOP SIGNS AT
  THE MAIN GATE ON PORTUGUESE BEND ROAD AND THE CREST ROAD
  GATE.

  Yolanta Schwartz explained that the purpose of proposed gate relocation is to improve safety.
  Yolanta Schwartz described the project design and identified the new locations of the proposed
  gates at Portuguese Bend and Crest Road entrances. It was explained that potential queuing could
  become problematic early in the morning. Construction staging parked at City Hall Campus and
  lined up to exit the parking lot and entered through the residents’ entrance.

  Vanessa Munoz described peak hour traffic and queuing. Northbound traffic would improve
  however, it could be problematic for people entering the City due to cars queuing on the road.
  Traffic queuing from the Campus would worsen but only temporarily, typical wait time would
  last 15-30 minutes. The proposed gate relocation would provide guards with better line of sight
  and would not create massive traffic back-up on Palos Verdes Drive North; but it would
  aggravate existing condition. The alternative solution would be to relocate guardhouse.

  Commissioner Virtue concerned about the turning radius from the Campus to the gate entrance.
  Vanessa Munoz recommended proper trigger to activate the gate.

  Chair Wilson was concerned about larger vehicles.

  Vanessa agreed that it could be a problem so she suggested maneuvering large vehicle to
  determine best location of loop trigger.

  Commissioner Raine was concerned with visitors merging with residential traffic and potential
  blind spot.

  It was explained by Vanessa Munoz that the stop sign should be able to mitigate the blind spot
  issue at the guest entrance.

  Kristen Raig explained that this project resulted from security consultant's study and that it would
  also help facilitate resident entry instead of waiting for security response after they have passed
  the window.

  Chair Wilson reiterated concern about the turning radius.

  Vanessa repeated that adjustments could be made in the field to accommodate larger vehicle's
  turning radius.

   Mark Grindle brought up safety factors of having the gate relocated. It would help security see
  inside cars especially when windows are tinted.

  Chair Wilson brought up that he was unaware the campus is being used for staging area.

  Mark Grindle explained how the campus is used and the daily average number of cars waiting
  before 7:00 AM. To expedite the entry process, security would check for clearance while drivers
  are parked waiting to enter the gate. Traffic control is managed well with little impact to residents.
  Peak time is between 7:00 and 7:10 AM.

  Motion by Commissioner Raine and seconded by Commissioner Virtue to go to Council.

  AYES:  Commissioners: Margeta, Raine, Virtue and Chairman Wilson

1.  CALL TO ORDER

  A regular meeting of the Traffic Commission of the City of Rolling Hills was called to order by
  Chair Wilson at 8:30a.m. on Thursday, July 23, 2020 via teleconference.

2.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Bobit, Raine, Virtue and Chair Wilson. Ty Bobit
  Commissioners Absent:  Margeta
  Others Present:  Elaine Jeng, City Manager
  Meredith T. Elguira, Planning & Community Services Director
  Vanessa Munoz, Traffic Engineer
  Deputy Tami Bouse
  Captain James Powers
  Jane Abzug, Assistant Attorney

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  NONE.

4.  PRESENTATION

  A.  PRESENTATION OF NEW TRAFFIC COMMISSION TY BOBIT.

  Our New traffic commission member Bobit, replaces Commission Hawkins who is no
  longer on the board. Commission Bobit recently retired and gave a brief background of
  his career and experience. He is also a longtime resident of the City, since 1991.

  B.  PRESENTATION BY REPRESENTATIVES OF THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  SHERIFF’S DEPARTMENT, LOMITA STATION, ON TRAFFIC STATISTICS
  FOR THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS.

  Deputy Bouse opened by stating that traffic has been very light since the beginning of
  2020. Therefore, no supplemental traffic enforcement statistics are available for the
  month of January. For month of February, the Sheriff’s concentrated their effort on Crest
  Road and Eastfield, there were 12 citations (6 speed and 6 stop). For March, the Sheriff’s
  concentrated their efforts on Crest Road and Portuguese Bend Road, stating there were
  18 reported violations, 15 of which were speed related. For both April and May there
  was very little traffic and no activity reported, due to Covid-19 and the stay home order.
  Therefore, the Sheriff’s department will not bill Rolling Hills for both April and May of
  2020. Deputy Bouse stated that during both months, they did come in and out of the City
  several times, but no violations were observed. The month of June, the Sheriff’s
  concentrated their efforts on Portuguese Bend Road and Eastfield, however they reported
  -1-  10
   traffic remained light. But there were 5 reported traffic enforcement violations, 2 of which
  were speed related.

  Commissioner Virtue asked, if in general the sheriff’s department found it to be true or
  have noticed more drivers’ driving at a higher rate of speed due to the lighter traffic we
  are experiencing. Deputy Bouse responded that has not been noticed, so no that is not
  true.

5.  OLD BUSINESS

  NONE.

6.  NEW BUSINESS

  NONE.

8.  MATTERS FROM MEMBERS OF THE TRAFFIC COMMISSION

  Community Association presentation on volume of delivery vehicles, provided by Mark Grindle,
  Gate Supervisor.

  A. DISCUSS THE INCREASE IN VOLUME OF DELIVERY VEHICLES INTERING
  ROLLING HILLS. (COMMISSION BOBIT)

  Commissioner Bobit has heard through the association and from several residents but mainly
  from the Caballeros side, that riders have experienced unsafe traffic conditions while riding.
  During his conversations he recognized the repeated comments that truck drivers were not
  giving horseback riders the right of way. Rolling Hills is an equestrian community, but
  because the truck and delivery drivers are probably not residents of the City, therefore may
  not be aware of the horses’ need to feel safe.

  Commissioner Bobit reviewed the statistics of delivery trucks that entered the City for both
  2019 & 2020, that were provided by Mr. Grindle. He noted there was an increase of delivery
  trucks overall in 2020 from 2019, with a significant increase beginning in April, a 68 %
  increase May an 84 % increase, June had a 73 % increase, from 2019. The increase of parcel
  and food delivery, as well as the significant reduction of traffic coincides with the beginning
  of Covid-19 and the stay at home order.

  During a conversation Commissioner Bobit was having with the Community Association
  they expressed their concern of what they could do to bring better awareness to the delivery
  drivers and the importance understanding and providing safety for the riders, horses and
  walkers. The Association printed leaflets read “Caution if you see horses, please stop or
  drive very slowly and pass when safe to do so”. The leaflets were given to the gate attendants
  for handout to the non-regular truck drivers with the idea that the regular drivers are familiar

Minutes
Traffic Commission
07-23-2020
  -2-  11
   with horse and pedestrian rights of way and the crossings. However, it has also been
  reported that a Fed Ex truck sped right by a group of women and did not slowdown in any
  way. It is unclear how many or how aggressively the leaflets were handed out. To date,
  their effectiveness is not yet known. Commissioner Bobit stated that since the “stay home”
  order was issued he has also noticed an increase of walkers within the City, suggesting the
  leaflets be reworked to include walkers. In addition, several people have mentioned that
  truck drivers do not seem to move over in the other lane and provide a safe distance between
  the truck while passing walkers, even when there is no oncoming traffic.

  Commissioner Bobit suggested a quarterly reminder to drivers to provide the right of way
  to horse riders and pedestrians and slow down when passing or stop if there is oncoming
  traffic, then pass slowly and providing adequate room when passing, especially when driving
  on Crest Road.

  Captain Powers reinforced that one of the most important things the City can do is to educate
  it residents and entering delivery drivers and guests. This can be done through letters,
  leaflets at the gate or signage at the gate and/or on the streets within Rolling Hills. He also
  stated that walkers would be safest if they walked in the direction of oncoming traffic and
  not with traffic, allowing them to see any cars coming towards them.

  Commissioner Virtue mentioned this it has been her experience that the City’s residents’
  attitude is such, that animals, people, and horses are free to roam back and forth across the
  streets. Therefore, it is important that the delivery drivers clearly understand their
  responsibility to observe their speed and drive cautiously. Commissioner Virtue re-
  emphasized the importance of notifying all drivers, especially newer delivery drivers and
  the elderly residents, which she believes they drive too fast any. The regular drivers may
  know where they are going, they still tend to drive very fast. She expressed the importance
  of educating drivers, of the number of people within the city, how many walker’s and bike
  riders there are, in addition to the horseback riders, be included in the flyers.

  Chair Wilson stated this might be a good time to bring back the use of an unmanned police
  car, due to its effectiveness of keeping speeds down, especially on Crest or even on
  Portuguese Road. Commissioners Bobit, Raine, and Virtue, all expressed supporting the
  idea. Chair Wilson wanted to know what one would be cited for if failing to pass at a safe
  distance or too close to an animal or person when pass or not give the right of way to
  horseback riders or pedestrians.

  Captain Powers briefly mentioned there are pros and cons of an unmanned car and the length
  of time left at one location, such as vandalism to the unmanned car. He also reported that
  general people drive too fast, and even if speed is not the primary cause of a collision, it is
  usually an associated factor.

  Traffic Engineer Munoz recalled that Commissioner Hawkins wanted to add language to the
  Municipal Code 10.36 regarding the protection of animals not only at crossings but
  throughout the streets and not just for equestrian sightings. She suggested that maybe this
  additional language could be used when citing unsafe drivers but cannot recall if completed
  or implemented. Commissioner Virtue does not recall implementing the additional language

Minutes
Traffic Commission
07-23-2020
  -3-  12
   because at that time some sentences were dropped, and others were being added, and cannot
  recall if it was ever completed.

  City Manager Jeng also recalls that there was some proposed language and the proposed
  language came back to the Traffic Commission several times, as well as offline
  conversations were held. She believes that at one time Commissioner Hawkins was satisfied
  with other areas of the municipal code, did not push through to completion, is her
  recollection

  Commissioner Raines stated, he has no problem with pedestrians walking in the street and
  it is what he enjoys about living in the City.

  Captain Powers mentioned that the Community Association has identified locations where
  the easements need to be cleared back to 8 feet. Once cleared, this will allow more room
  for the walkers to walk out of the way of traffic.

  Chair Wilson expressed the need to stay aware of traffic within the City, to ensure the safety
  of its residents, horseback rides and all other domestic animals that are free to roam.

  Commissioner Virtue stated that something she sees more and more on Crest Rd. That when
  there are dogs on both sides of the street eventually the dogs want to greet each other and
  run into the middle of the street and cause the traffic to stop in both directions. Therefore,
  speeding is a significant hazard, especially on Crest Road. She supports the direction of
  educating the residents, truck and delivery drivers, through flyers, leaflets, and newsletter.

  Commissioner Bobit stated that he would talk with the Community Association about re-
  working the leaflets to include walkers and all animals. He will also ask that they be more
  aggressive in their distribution to all incoming trucks, guests or non-residents, at least for a
  while.

  Deputy Bouse responded to Chair Wilsons’ earlier question, “what would a driver be cited
  for?” Had they not passed at a safe distance or driven too close the horses or pedestrians.
  She said that Municipal Code 10.62.020, refers to reckless driving and could be cited if it
  was truly reckless.

  Chair Wilson opened the item to public comment. No comments from the public were
  received.

  Chair Wilson stated that he knows horses and spends a lot time around them and knows that
  certain horses can be more skittish then others, so when he comes upon a horse when driving,
  especially on Portuguese Bend Road, he is very cautious to not scare them. He pointed out
  that even going 30 miles an hour over the bumps can really scare the horses, so drivers do
  have to learn to be careful and aware of this. Therefore, its very important to remind trucks
  and delivery drivers, who may not be around horses and will require on going reminders.
  Commissioner Bobit mentioned he recently notice how many signs there are already at the
  gates and believes that posting too many signs, makes them all ineffective or invisible.

   City Manager Jeng stated that the City has recently deployed the 2019-2020 Stripping
  Project, which include delineation striping for horse crossing. They have identified 30 horse
  crossings, 15 of which were existing and only required sprucing up plus 15 new crossing
  were also added. At the existing crossing’s there were signs already posted, identifying the
  “Horse Crossing”. These signs were also posted at the newly added crossings and at the
  code required height. She also stated that ability to cite a driver for reckless driving would
  be difficult for the sheriff’s department because it requires their visual observation,
  therefore, it may be more effective to come from the point of view of behavior change or
  modification. She stated that she would contract Kristen to discuss an effective approach.
